new_statements.quote: Sie sprachen äusserst schnell und ihre, an Nasentönen reiche, Sprache klang mir widrig. Die Betonung, verstärkt oder geschwächt, schien auch bei ihnen, wie bei vielen andern Stämmen, verschiedene Zeiten und Personen zu bezeichnen.
new_statements.translation: They spoke extremely fast, and their language, rich in nasal sounds, sounded disagreeable to me. The accentuation, strengthened or weakened, seemed with them too, as with many other tribes, to mark different tenses and persons.
new_statements.citation: Spix, Johann Baptist von & Martius, Carl Friedrich Philipp von. 1831. Reise in Brasilien auf Befehl Sr. Majestät Maximilian Joseph I., Königs von Baiern, in den Jahren 1817 bis 1820 gemacht und beschrieben. Dritter Theil. München: M. Lindauer. p. 1202.
new_statements.locator: Dritter Theil, p. 1202 (Missouri Botanical Garden scan, PDF page 324), account of S. Antonio de Maripi on the Japurá, c. Jan. 1820; repeated almost verbatim in Martius 1867, Beiträge I, p. 478
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Files checked under (1) Quote: the page image p. 1202 of Spix & Martius 1831, Reise in Brasilien III, Missouri Botanical Garden scan) carries, verbatim, lines 22-25 of the page: "Sie sprachen äusserst schnell und ihre, an Nasentönen reiche, Sprache klang mir widrig. Die Betonung, verstärkt oder geschwächt, schien auch bei ihnen, wie bei vielen andern Stämmen, verschiedene Zeiten und Personen zu bezeichnen." The scanned ( lines 14941-14947) matches; the following page (p. 1203, the scanned text) has "Seine Ausdrücke hierüber in der eigenen Sprache waren sehr einfach; er wiederholte sich oft, und schien ohne Wechsel der Zeiten und Personen zu reden", as the reader says, plus a footnote giving…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No placement rule exists. The only remark on accent in any source is Martius's 1820 ear-witness impression that variations in accentuation ('Betonung'), stronger or weaker, seemed to distinguish tenses and persons — i.e. that accent might be grammatically contrastive — which he undercuts on the next page (p. 1203: Gregorio 'seemed to speak without change of tenses and persons'). The only lexical data, the c. 200-item Latin-glossed list in Martius 1867 II pp. 273-275, carries acute accents in mixed positions (final nühó, coisé, ucumá, cuirá, coiná; penult hacoámö, cohóme, gotlövúna, jáme; antepenult acópima), and the volume's only definition of the acute (p. 29, Tupi introduction) says it either 'sharpens the vowel' or 'stresses the syllable', so the marks cannot be read as stress with confidence.
new_statements.exceptions: None; no rule is given from which exceptions could arise. Martius 1867 II p. 273 fn. notes only 'Das Praefixum possessivum scheint hier Co.'
new_statements.domain_note: Impressionistic remark on running speech by a naturalist-traveller, not a phonological description; no word-vs-phrase distinction; the wordlist forms are elicited citation forms, many with a possessive prefix co-.
new_statements.identity_note: Coeruna = Koeruna / Coëruna / Coeuruna (Martius's spellings; Glottolog coer1236, 'Unclassified Huitotoan' unun9983 under Huitotoan huit1251; ASJP doculect COERUNA is the same Martius list). The entire attestation is one wordlist taken c. January 1820 at S. Antonio de Maripi on the Japurá from the Coeruna principal Gregorio, via Lingua Geral interpretation, printed in Martius 1867 II pp. 273-275 (Wikipedia's 'pp. 325-326' is wrong for this scan). No dialect question arises; the language was already reduced to c. 100 aldeia residents in 1820 and Loukotka 1968 reports the villages Portuguese-speaking.
